title: Charged photon trapping and extremal scaling

items.title: RN circular null radius and exterior instability

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: PDF pp. 50–51: the Schwarzschild null effective potential, its photon-sphere maximum at 3GM/c^2 and radial instability. Section 6.2.5, printed pp. 266–268 (PDF pp. 273–275), treats the distinct extremal RN throat limit. Tong's charge normalization is not imported.

references.title: Max Weissenbacher, Decay and non-decay for the massless Vlasov equation on subextremal and extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 248, 118 (2024)
references.locator: arXiv:2303.15338v2, Section 1.3.5, equation (35), for the surface-gravity definition; Section 2.1, equations (45)–(48), for the local surface-gravity formula, photon-sphere radius, and Schwarzschild/extremal special cases; Sections 2.3.1–2.3.5 for conserved geodesic quantities and null trapping. The paper's geodesic-flow estimates are not used as the proof here.

items.statement:
Let $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$, and assume $0\le Q^2<m^2$. Use the asymptotically flat dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric with $M=m$ and $f(r)=1-2m/r+Q^2/r^2$ on the exterior $r>r_+:=m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$. Here $r_-$ denotes the other algebraic horizon root $m-\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$; when $Q^2>0$, $r_\pm$ are the local null Killing horizons of the selected RN model, and when $Q^2=0$, $r_+=2m$ is the larger root. An equatorial circular null geodesic means a smooth nonconstant affinely parametrized geodesic $\gamma(s)=(x^0(s),r_c,\pi/2,\phi(s))$ with $g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=0$ and nonzero angular momentum $\ell=r_c^2\dot\phi$. Its effective radial function is $h(r)=f(r)/r^2$. The outer circular null radius is

$$r_{\mathrm{ph}+}=\frac{3m+\sqrt{9m^2-8Q^2}}{2}.$$

It lies strictly above $r_+$ and is a strict local maximum of $h$. Along an equatorial geodesic, define the conserved quantities $E:=f(r)\dot x^0$ and $\ell:=r^2\dot\phi$. At fixed $E,\ell$, the null radial geodesic equation is $\ddot r=-\tfrac12\ell^2h'(r)$. Its radial linearization at $r=r_{\mathrm{ph}+}$, defined by writing $r=r_{\mathrm{ph}+}+\epsilon\rho(s)$ and retaining the terms of first order in $\epsilon$, is $\ddot\rho-\nu^2\rho=0$, where $\nu^2:=-\tfrac12\ell^2h''(r_{\mathrm{ph}+})>0$; it has the growing mode $\rho(s)=e^{\nu s}$. The other algebraic stationary radius is $r_{\mathrm{ph}-}=(3m-\sqrt{9m^2-8Q^2})/2$; this proposition assigns it no exterior-orbit interpretation. Coordinates $x^0,r,m,q_e,q_m$ have length units, angular coordinates are dimensionless, and the affine parameter has arbitrary normalization. This is a null-ray calculation for the exact RN metric; it proves no wave-decay or Morawetz estimate.

items.title: Extremal dyonic RN throat as a local scaled limit

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: Section 6.2.5, printed pp. 266–268 (PDF pp. 273–275), derives the extremal RN throat metric as AdS2 × S2. The exact pullback of the Maxwell two-form and all-derivative compact convergence are proved here.

references.title: Lars Aalsma, Jan Pieter van der Schaar and Manus R. Visser, Extremal black hole decay in de Sitter space, JHEP 07 (2024) 259, arXiv:2311.13742
references.locator: Section 2.1, equations (2.4)–(2.11), PDF pp. 4–5, gives the extremal RN metric and an independent near-horizon coordinate scaling. Its units and charge convention are not imported.

items.statement:
Let $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, set the RN mass parameter $M=m$, and use the exact dyonic RN metric and two-form on $r>m$. For each dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define $\Phi_\lambda(T,R,\omega)=(x^0=T/\lambda,\ r=m+\lambda R,\ \omega)$ on $D=\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$. Then

$$g_\lambda:=\Phi_\lambda^*g=-\frac{R^2}{(m+\lambda R)^2}\,dT^2+\frac{(m+\lambda R)^2}{R^2}\,dR^2+(m+\lambda R)^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_\lambda:=\Phi_\lambda^*\mathcal F=-\frac{q_e}{(m+\lambda R)^2}\,dT\wedge dR+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$

As $\lambda\downarrow0$, the pair converges with every coordinate derivative uniformly on each compact subset of $D$ to

$$g_0=-\frac{R^2}{m^2}\,dT^2+\frac{m^2}{R^2}\,dR^2+m^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_0=-\frac{q_e}{m^2}\,dT\wedge dR+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$

Here $x^0,r,T,R,m,q_e,q_m$ have length units, $\lambda$ is dimensionless, and $\gamma_{S^2},\omega_{S^2}$ are the unit round metric and outward area form. “Convergence with every coordinate derivative uniformly on compact subsets” means that, in a finite smooth atlas, every coordinate derivative of each tensor coefficient converges uniformly on each compact subset. The convergence is only on $R>0$: it asserts neither extension through $R=0$, uniform control over the whole original exterior, nor a decoupled theory. In the positive-electric subcase $q_e=m$, $q_m=0$, the displayed pullbacks agree exactly with the inherited near-horizon theorem's field and metric formulas.

items.title: Subextremal RN surface gravity has no uniform positive lower bound

references.title: Max Weissenbacher, Decay and non-decay for the massless Vlasov equation on subextremal and extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 248, 118 (2024)
references.locator: arXiv:2303.15338v2, Section 1.3.5, equation (35), for the surface-gravity definition; Section 2.1, equation (45), for the surface-gravity formula and subextremal/extremal distinction, with equations (47)–(48) listing the Schwarzschild and extremal RN special cases. The exact root formula and uniform-lower-bound counterexample are proved here.

items.statement: Fix a mass length $m>0$. For each length parameter $q_e\in\mathbb R$ with $0<q_e^2<m^2$, take the electric RN family with mass parameter $M=m$ and magnetic parameter $q_m=0$, and define $Q^2:=q_e^2$, $r_\pm:=m\pm\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$, and $\kappa_+(q_e):=(r_+-r_-)/(2r_+^2)$. The false claim is that there exists a constant $c>0$, with units of inverse length, such that $\kappa_+(q_e)\ge c$ for every such $q_e$.
